observations.observation: The selected query for identity4 is a light SUV, with a tree near its body; candidate identities129/199 and same-ID positives show different viewpoints and illumination. Some same-ID RGB images are much darker than the query.
observations.inference: Viewpoint, occlusion and illumination differences coexist with similar overall body appearance. This does not establish which cue the model used.

observations.observation: Identity6 and identity10 examples are both reddish sedans in visible light. Selected queries/positives/negatives include front, rear and side views, and bright visible/NIR reflections in some frames.
observations.inference: These pairs combine similar overall appearance with large view changes; treating all their errors as a single missing local-detail problem is not supported.

observations.observation: Identity8 and identity34 include light sedans with similar global silhouettes. Rear lamps, body/window shapes and perspectives differ among the selected examples; backgrounds and partial occlusion also vary.
observations.inference: Preserving localized evidence is a testable direction, but sheets do not demonstrate that a frequency expert can extract or generalize it.

observations.observation: Selected harmed/both-wrong cases include front-to-rear matches, dark visible frames, stronger NIR/thermal visibility and backgrounds with other cars or trees. Some wrong candidates have visibly different body categories.
observations.inference: The sample contains more than same-model near duplicates. A universal fine-detail-only explanation would be too narrow.

observations.observation: Native source crops vary in size; RGB,NIR,TIR are separately captured views. Sheets preserve aspect ratio within display cells, without spatial registration.
observations.inference: No pixel-perfect cross-modal regional correspondence, sensor timing, true thermal temperature, label correction or image alignment is established by this inspection.
